full_judgment: 6. Mr. A. H. Chowdhury, does not agree that the Bangladesh Transfer of Immovable Property (Temporary Provision) Order, and the Registration Act are two different statutes having conflicting provisions for registration of documents of the kind referred to. He has contended that the former is an amendary law enacted to amend certain provisions of the latter for a "temporary" period and that both should be read and construed as a single legislation. The P. O. 142/72 does not expressly seek to amend the Registration Act nor does it make any reference to it, and according to its title and nomenclature it is an independent aid separate law. But its operative part relates to registration of documents of transfer of immovable property. Registration of document and transfer of immovable property is also the rain subject, of the Registration Act which was enacted much earlier and was (and still is) in full force when the later statute was enacted. Procedure of registration of such documents has been exhaustively laid. down in the ‘existing' statute, namely the earlier statute and this procedure has not been 'touched by the later statute... But the later statute has prescribed an additional requirement of an affidavit. In view of this fact we are inclined to hold that the later statute is, by necessary implication, an amendatory law enacted for amending the existing law regarding registration in respect of immovable property only.
